case_name: Collector of Thanjavur Distt. and Others v S. Rajagopalan and Others
petitioner: Collector of Thanjavur Distt. and Others
facts: This is an appeal filed by the Collector of District, the Special Commissioner and Secretary to Government of Tamil Nadu.
There are five respondents in this appeal.
The writ petition was filed by respondents 1 to 4 in the High Court of Madras, the same being transferred to the Administrative Tribunal of Tamil Nadu.

The list of Deputy Tahsildars for the years 1982 was drawn by the Collector Thanjavur on 7.2.1983 and the said list did not contain the names of the writ petitioners (respondents 1 to 4 in this appeal).
Their names were omitted on the ground that minor punishment was imposed on them consequent to disciplinary enquiry.
The respondents questioned the non-inclusion of their names in the panel before the Tribunal.
issues: Whether the non-inclusion of the respondents (writ petitioners) in the selected list of Deputy Tahsildars for the year 1982 would amount to a second punishment on them.

Whether the Tribunal was correct in thinking that if the minor punishments inflicted on the respondents were taken into consideration at the time of considering their merit for the purpose of inclusion in the list of Deputy Tahsildars, that would amount to double jeopardy.
petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Tribunal was in error in thinking that the non-inclusion of the respondents (writ petitioners) in the above selected list of Deputy Tahsildars would amount to a second punishment on them.

Learned counsel for the appellant contends that this view of the Tribunal is incorrect in view of the decision of this Court in Union of India and others v. K. V. Jankiraman and others, 1991 (4) SCC 109: JT 1991 (3) SC 527 1991 Indlaw SC 1034.
court_reasoning: The Tribunal has erred in holding that when an officer is found guilty in the discharge of his duties, an imposition of penalty is all that is necessary to improve his conduct and to enforce, discipline and ensure purity in the administration.
An employee has no right to promotion. He has only a right to be considered for promotion.
The least that is expected of any administration is that it does not reward an employee with promotion retrospectively from a date when for his conduct before that date he is penalised in praesenti.
holding: We hold that the Tribunal was in error in granting the direction to which we have referred to herein before.

The direction granted by the Tribunal to consider the case of the respondents/Assistants for inclusion in the panel of Deputy Tahsildar of 1982 uninfluenced by the punishment on them is hereby set aside.

It is, therefore, open to the competent authority to consider the cases of the respondents (who have not since retired) by taking into consideration the fact that the minor punishments were imposed on the said respondents during the relevant period.
